name: Kuthampully Handloom
tagline: Kerala’s kasavu masters — handwoven white-and-gold sarees, mundus and dhotis
summary: Historic handloom cluster famous for Kuthampully kasavu sarees, set mundu and double mundu; GI‑protected craftsmanship, cooperative tradition and village weaving visits.
description: Kuthampully Handloom refers to the handweaving cluster centred on Kuthampully village, famous for cream (off‑white) cotton garments with gold-coloured kasavu borders — sarees, set mundu and double dhotis. The craft traces to Devanga weavers brought to the region by the old Kochi rulers; the product later gained a Geographical Indication (GI).

The village functions through a cooperative tradition (Kuthampully Handloom Industrial Co‑operative Society, formed in 1972) and family looms. Weaving uses traditional pit / handlooms and jacquard patterns; finished pieces are prized for texture, simple elegance and durability.

Visitors can watch weaving, learn about kasavu technique, buy directly from co‑op outlets and small shops, and support weavers by choosing GI‑marked and cooperative-supplied pieces. Confirm opening times and stock with shops before you travel.
highlights: Kuthampully sarees and fine cotton fabrics hold a GI registration (certificate issued 4 Sep 2010).
Traditional kasavu look: cream/off‑white cloth with gold‑coloured (zari‑style) borders.
Village cooperative created in 1972; craft passed down through Devanga weaving families.
Products include sarees, set mundu (mundum neriyathum), double mundu/veshti and dhotis.
Good place to see handloom processes and buy directly from weavers and cooperative outlets.

sections.heading: Background
body: Kuthampully’s weaving tradition goes back centuries; local accounts and state craft documentation say Devanga (Devengas) weavers were invited from the old Mysore region by Kochi rulers and settled here. Over time the village developed a distinct kasavu weaving style for ceremonial and everyday Kerala dress.

The industry organised itself through the Kuthampully Handloom Industrial Co‑operative Society (registered 1972). The Kuthampully products — sarees, set mundu and double dhoti/mundu — are recognised under a Geographical Indication (GI) registration to protect their identity and traditional methods.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Walk the lanes to see pit and frame looms, the jacquard designing and finishing of kasavu borders. Many households still operate looms; cooperative outlets and small showrooms demonstrate weaving and sell finished pieces.

Shop for authentic Kuthampully kasavu sarees, set mundu and double mundu — ask for cooperative outlets or GI‑marked products to avoid powerloom imitations. Some local shops and newer marketplaces also list Kuthampully pieces online (confirm authenticity when buying).

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Kuthampully lies on the Bharathapuzha and serves visitors travelling between Thrissur, Ottapalam and Palakkad. Nearest major railhead is Shoranur (about 29 km); the nearest large airport is Cochin International (≈93 km). Travel by road from Ottapalam/Palakkad is the usual approach; local directions and times vary — confirm before you travel.

If you want demonstrations or a guided visit, contact the cooperative or local DTPC/ tourism office ahead of arrival. Onam and Vishu season bring peak demand and many shops open extended hours — good for festive shopping but expect crowds; quieter months (Oct–Mar) are best for relaxed visits.

latest.text: News coverage of Onam 2026 reported high seasonal trade in Kuthampully kasavu shops as customers buy festival outfits.
Kerala government updates show the Free Handloom School Uniform scheme (2025–26) continues to bolster demand for local handloom clusters, supporting weavers including Kuthampully producers.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–March for pleasant weather; Onam (Aug–Sep) and Vishu (April) are busiest for shopping.
visitorInfo.howToReach: By road from Ottapalam/Palakkad; nearest railhead Shoranur ~29 km, nearest major airport Cochin International ~93 km. Local taxis and buses connect; confirm schedules before travel.
etiquette: Ask for GI‑registered or cooperative outlets and the Kuthampully cooperative when buying to reduce risk of powerloom substitutes.
Bargain politely; many weavers sell directly and prices reflect handwork — higher for pure handloom and pure‑zari borders.
If you want demonstrations or bulk buying, contact the cooperative or a shop in advance to confirm availability and timing.
Respect looms and workspaces — ask before photographing weavers at work and avoid disturbing the process.
